mainEntity.name: Do I need an external audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: External audit is mandatory for large proprietary companies, some trusts, and many not-for-profits above size thresholds. It may also be required by a lender, regulator, or constitution. If you are unsure whether you need one, the matched firm assesses your obligations — or if you know you need one, tell us the type and we will match accordingly.

mainEntity.name: Can the same firm do my tax and my audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Independence rules restrict this — a firm that prepares your accounts generally cannot also sign the external audit (there are limited exceptions). Our matched firms either arrange a separate independent auditor on your behalf or, where permitted, use a separate team within the firm. For SMSF audits, a fully independent auditor is always used.

mainEntity.name: How much does an external audit cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Audit fees depend on entity size, complexity, and the state of the records. A straightforward small-company audit may be $5,000–$12,000; complex or multi-entity audits are higher. The matched firm gives you a clear quote after reviewing your situation — the matching itself is free.

mainEntity.name: How quickly will a matched audit firm contact me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched firm will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance to discuss your audit needs.

mainEntity.name: Can an audit firm help with a special-purpose or grant audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched firm scopes special-purpose audits for lenders, grant bodies or regulators — tailored to your specific purpose rather than a generic template, so you meet the funder's requirements efficiently.

mainEntity.name: Can an audit firm help with due diligence before an acquisition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched firm performs financial due diligence on acquisition targets — verifying the numbers, identifying risks and contingent liabilities, and giving you confidence (or a renegotiation lever) before you commit.

mainEntity.name: Is audit and assurance matching free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matching service is free for businesses. We are engaged by the accounting firms in our network, not by you. You are under no obligation to proceed with any matched firm, and the matched firm gives you a clear quote before any work begins.

mainEntity.name: Can an audit firm help with not-for-profit or charity audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched firm handles not-for-profit and charity audits — ensuring ACNC compliance, meeting constitutional audit requirements, and maintaining your charitable registration and grant eligibility.

blocks.heading: Audit & Assurance — what we can help with
blocks.text: SPECIALIST NETWORKAudit & Assurance — what we can help withStatutory external auditLarge proprietary companies, disclosed-trust companies, superannuation funds (via the SMSF auditor), and many not-for-profits require an external audit by a registered company auditor. Our network includes firms with the ASIC auditor registration needed to sign these reports. Tell us in the questionnaire which kind of audit you need and we will match accordingly.Internal and special-purpose auditsNot every audit is statutory. You may need an internal audit to strengthen controls, a special-purpose audit for a lender or grant body, a due-diligence audit before an acquisition, or a compliance audit for a regulator. Our matched firms scope these engagements to your specific purpose — not a generic template.Independence and qualityAudit independence is not optional — it is a legal and ethical requirement. Our matched firms maintain independence from the preparation of the accounts they audit (or coordinate a separate team within the firm where permitted). For SMSF audits, a fully independent external auditor is used. You never need to source the auditor yourself.
